text.p: These are the leading stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- S E R B I A -
NASA BORBA

- Special U.S. envoy for former Yugoslavia Robert Gelbard says after talks with Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic the United States is seriously concerned over Milosevic's said inability to extradite war crimes indictees who are in Serbia to The Hague.
- Serbian government and Italy's STET still negotiating purchase of PTT Serbia telecommunications. Signing officially postponed for "technical reasons".
- Health and social workers strike continues despite progress in talks with government over payment of late wages.
- Serbian teachers in 106 out of Serbia's 242 schools on strike.
- Yugoslav and Croatian foreign ministers, Milan Milutinovic and Mate Granic, to sign consular convention and initial agreements on mutual legal assistance in Zagreb.
POLITIKA

- Serbian President Milosevic says in talks with U.S. envoy Gelbard Yugoslavia is interested in developing comprehensive relations and cooperation with all countries, including speedier advancing of bilateral ties with the U.S.

- Yugoslav deputy prime minister Nikola Sainovic says after visit to Kuwait the two countries have agreed to intensify all forms of cooperation, Kuwait to urge Yugoslavia's return to international financial institutions.
- Sevojno copper rolling mill expects $2 million per year from effects of European Union trade preferentials for Yugoslavia.
- Montenegrin shipping company Jugooceanija records $3 million in profit in the first four months of the year.
- Bosnian Serb and Moslem state commissions for missing persons no closer to agreement on searches for bodies of killed civilians and soldiers on each other's territories.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Biggest supplier of meat and meat products to Yugoslav capital Belgrade BIM Slavija in total blockade since August, account in the red more than 61 million dinars.
BORBA
- Serbia's MIN engine factory of Nis and Serb Sarajevo authorities sign nine million German marks agreement to build and equip 19 factories in the Bosnian Serb Republic moved from Sarajevo.
POLITIKA EKSPRES

- Split in opposition coalition Zajedno (together) widening. Coalition leaders Zoran Djindjic and Vuk Draskovic no longer speak the same language and it only remains for them to technically bury the coalition, says state news agency Tanjug.
- M O N T E N E G R O -
POBJEDA

- Montenegrin state delegation on visit to The Hague War Crime Tribunal at invitation of chief prosecutor Louis Arbour. Delegation includes state prosecutor Vlado Susovic, deputy foreign minister Veselin Sukovic and Podgorica public prosecutor Vlado Vukovic.
- Republican parliament session resumes. Agenda includes draft on parliamentary commission for monitoring security police.
- Minimum May salary, agreed by trade unions, trade chamber and government, 320 dinars, unchanged from April.

- Montenegrin state TV will introduce one-hour daily Albanian-language broadcasts at the initiative of Democratic Union of Albanians party. TV Montenegro will also open office in Ulcinj. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
